# CookieDeletionScopeMismatch

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Cookie deletion must target the same path and domain as creation. Use the original scope when expiring the cookie.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
setcookie("auth","token",["path"=>"/app"]); setcookie("auth","",["expires"=>1,"path"=>"/"]);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Delete the cookie using its original path and domain.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Two resolved cookie setters (`setcookie`/`setrawcookie`) are consecutive statements and use the same literal name; the first stores a nonempty literal value, the second clears the value with a known positive expiry <=1. Highlight the deletion call when their scopes definitely differ:
  - the paths are both explicit nonempty literals and are not the same string, or
  - the domains are both explicit nonempty literals and still differ after lower-casing and dropping one leading dot.
- Path and domain are read from the options array when the third argument is a literal array, otherwise from the fourth/fifth (or named `path`/`domain`) arguments. Option names are matched case-insensitively, as PHP does. The scalar form is proven when the third argument is absent or a known integer, or when a `path`, `domain`, `secure` or `httponly` argument is present (PHP refuses those next to an options array); the stored cookie's expiry may then be any expression such as `time() + 3600`.
- Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods; user-defined lookalikes are excluded. Follow only bounded local proof in one lexical scope.
- Emit one finding per violating operation, not per supporting evidence statement. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Do not report unresolved or shadowed builtin names, unknown values, or incomplete receiver/type provenance. Unknown calls, aliases escaping, and intervening writes invalidate local proof. Similar code outside the stated detection contract is not a finding.
- An omitted or empty path or domain is not a definite scope: the browser derives it from the request. A setting omitted or empty on either side never makes that setting differ, so `setcookie("a", "v"); setcookie("a", "", 1, "/");` is not reported.
- Domains differing only by letter case or by a leading dot are the same scope.
- No report when a path or domain is not a literal string, when the third argument is neither a literal array nor a proven scalar expiry, when the options array has unknown keys, or when it spells one option name twice in different letter cases.
- Both standard suppression forms suppress this native ID.

## Fix

None. Choosing a repair requires intent or additional runtime information.

## PHP versions

Available throughout supported PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced builtin/extension is available. Respect syntax/version-specific receiver contracts; unavailable APIs are not this rule’s concern.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "CookieDeletionScopeMismatch": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore CookieDeletionScopeMismatch
```
